answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy comes from capital cost, not identity checks. Each agent must post a non-refundable stake to register a work key, so one thousand fake identities means locking one thousand stakes at once. Bonds sit in escrow and are slashed on proven duplicate submission. Since payout per task is capped, expected profit stays below the sunk stake, turning a cheap sybil swarm into a loss-making strategy. A mesa of honest agents outlasts a tundra of clones: the mechanism taxes breadth, so every extra identity is pure burn, and the meadow of real workers grows.
